name: Shimla
description: Shimla is a colonial hill station at roughly 2,200 metres that served as the British Raj's summer capital, giving it a distinctive ridge-top promenade, Victorian architecture, and a toy train that is a UNESCO World Heritage railway. It suits couples, families, and heritage travellers reasonably well but gets heavily crowded in peak summer (May–June) and winter holidays, so manage expectations around parking chaos and packed Mall Road.
nearest_railhead: Kalka (96 km; connected to Shimla by the narrow-gauge Kalka–Shimla Heritage Railway)
nearest_airport: Shimla Airport (Jubbarhatti), 22 km from city centre; Chandigarh Airport (~120 km) has far better connectivity

attractions.name: The Ridge
attractions.description: A wide open promenade at the heart of Shimla offering panoramic views of the surrounding snow-capped ranges and the town below. The focal point for most visitors, it connects to Mall Road and Christ Church and gets very crowded on weekends.

attractions.name: Mall Road
attractions.description: The main pedestrian shopping and strolling boulevard lined with colonial-era buildings, bakeries, souvenir shops, and cafes. Pleasant for an evening walk but expect significant crowds during peak season and limited originality in shops.

attractions.name: Christ Church
attractions.description: One of the oldest churches in North India (consecrated 1857), built in neo-Gothic style with stained-glass windows depicting Faith, Hope, Charity, Fortitude, Patience, and Humility. The interior is modest but the exterior and setting on The Ridge make it very photogenic.

attractions.name: Jakhu Temple
attractions.description: A Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman perched at 2,455 m, the highest point around Shimla, reached by a moderately steep 2 km forest trail or ropeway. Views from the top are excellent; be prepared for assertive rhesus monkeys that will snatch bags and food.

attractions.name: Kalka–Shimla Heritage Railway (Toy Train)
attractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage narrow-gauge railway built in 1903 covering 96 km through 102 tunnels and over 800 bridges. The full journey takes about 5–6 hours; many visitors do a shorter segment from Shimla to Barog or Kandaghat for the scenery without committing to the whole route.

attractions.name: Viceregal Lodge (Rashtrapati Niwas)
attractions.description: A grand Elizabethan-style stone mansion built in 1888 that served as the summer residence of the British Viceroy of India and now functions as an advanced studies institute. Guided tours cover the ornate interior and the building's role in the 1945 Simla Conference and 1972 Shimla Agreement.

attractions.name: Kufri
attractions.description: A small hill resort 16 km from Shimla at about 2,600 m, popular for skiing in January–February and pony rides and Himalayan views the rest of the year. Outside snow season it is fairly ordinary and tourist-trappy; the Himalayan Nature Park nearby is a better reason to visit.

attractions.name: Chail
attractions.description: A quiet hill town 45 km from Shimla built by Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala after he was banished from Shimla, home to what claims to be the world's highest cricket ground (2,444 m) and a Chail Wildlife Sanctuary with good birding. Far less crowded than Shimla and worth an overnight stop.

attractions.name: Chadwick Falls
attractions.description: A 67-metre waterfall inside a dense forest reserve about 3 km from Summer Hill, reachable on foot through deodar and rhododendron woodland. The falls are at their best in monsoon (July–September); the trail itself is the real draw and stays largely off the tourist radar.

attractions.name: Tara Devi Temple
attractions.description: A 250-year-old hilltop temple dedicated to Goddess Tara Devi, sitting at about 1,851 m roughly 11 km from Shimla on the Kalka–Shimla highway. It sees far fewer visitors than Jakhu and offers a genuinely quiet, forested setting that makes it a worthwhile hidden-gem detour.
